articles.title: Oil falls as Trump downplays prospect of escalation with Iran
articles.description: Oil prices fell due to President Trump's announcement regarding US military action against Iran, easing supply concerns. Brent crude futures dropped to $92.33 per barrel while WTI futures reached $86.50. Trump stated he would maintain a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz temporarily. OPEC's oil output increased in October, supported by higher production from Saudi Arabia and Kuwait.

articles.title: Oil Prices Today: Brent Near $92 After 16% Weekly Rout; Is $100 Oil A Thing Of The Past?
articles.description: Brent had fallen around 6% in the previous session, hitting its lowest level since late August, as investors weighed the possibility of a diplomatic resolution to the Middle East conflict against continued attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Rupee among Asia's top performing currencies as AI trade cools
articles.description: The Indian rupee has gained considerable strength in FY27, aided by increased foreign portfolio investor inflows. A notable decline in crude oil prices has also positively impacted the rupee's performance. Experts believe the Reserve Bank of India will manage the currency's appreciation to rebuild its foreign exchange reserves. Recent interventions in the currency market have capped further gains in the rupee.

articles.description: Petrol is retailing at ₹102.12 per litre, while diesel is priced at ₹95.20 per litre. The national capital continues to have relatively lower fuel prices compared to other metros.

articles.title: Foreign investors keep faith in 83 stocks despite prolonged India selloff
articles.description: Foreign portfolio investors have favored 83 companies, including LIC, ONGC, and Indian Bank, over the past four quarters. Despite foreign investors selling nearly $28 billion of Indian stocks, some companies saw increased holdings. Large-cap firms like Lupin and SAIL attracted more interest from FPIs during this period. Recent concerns over crude oil prices and inflation impacted the sentiment of foreign investors towards Indian equities.

articles.title: Brokerages turn bullish on India as inflows fuel rally
articles.description: Global brokerages HSBC, Citigroup, and Jefferies have upgraded their outlook on Indian equities. They cite improving earnings prospects and attractive valuations as key factors for this optimism. Recent foreign fund inflows and reduced oil prices further support this positive sentiment. Citigroup anticipates significant growth in the Nifty 50 by the end of 2027. Overall, Indian equities are poised for a sharp recovery in the coming years.
